schemaNote: ladders[rig].rungs[] = one clip per gait rung with natural speed, cycle, foot phases, loop quality, slip; *Bands[] = neighbour handoffs with playback rates and phase offsets. Speeds are in each rig's own bake scale plus "world" = one common factor for all rigs.

rigHeightM.source: KayKit mannequin mesh height (the v6 catalogue note says ~1.9 m for Rig_Medium; that is not the mesh top)

units.worldScaleRule: Georg 30.09: KayKit proportions, one factor for all rigs, Rig_Medium = 1.5 m -> 1.5/2.204

method.evaluator: own glTF evaluator (numpy) on the exact library/KayKit GLBs; cross-checked against Blender 5.0 import (same foot positions, feet stay on footprint markers in the review scene)
method.cycle: first to last key; library loops repeat the first pose as last key, so the cycle is frames-1. The v6 catalogue durationSec counts that duplicated frame, so catalogue speeds read ~3 % low.
method.naturalSpeed: root-motion clips: hips travel per cycle / cycle time. In-place clips: median backward speed of the planted heel/toe in the body frame (= the ground speed at which the feet do not slide).
method.contacts: a heel (foot bone) or toe joint is planted while within 1.2 % of rig height above its own lowest point; footDownPhase = first frame of each contact / cycle
method.slip: max horizontal creep of a planted joint while played at natural speed; joint counts as planted only while also slower than max(0.15 m/s scaled, 25 % of speed). Threshold PASS <= 2.0 % of rig height (stated by this lane, research: Holden contact rules).
method.handoff: geometric mean of neighbour speeds (equal stretch both sides); playbackRateWindow = band edges / natural speed; flag when outside 0.75..1.25
method.phaseOffset: (leftFootDownPhase of target - of source) mod 1: start the target clip at source normalized time + offset so the same foot is down

motionLabV1Comparison.note: Stop rule check. Same clip, different definition: Motion Lab v1 uses the ankle only and a wide contact window (min + max(1.2 % height, 22 % of foot height range)), which pulls the median down. Re-running its exact method here gives 0.648 / 2.702 (Medium) and 1.747 / 2.590 (Large) against its reported 0.611 / 2.480 / 1.772 / 1.850. Medium and Large walk agree within 10 %; Large Running_A does not (40 %), reason unknown (Motion Lab measured the Black Knight actor). The ladder uses the strict no-slip speed.
